chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Nasr al-Khath'ami who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever recognises that we do not say except the truth, let him be content with what he knows from us. And if he hears from us something contrary to what he knows, let him know that it is a defence from us on his behalf.'

key_terms.حَقًّا: The truth — meaning the authoritative religious teaching that reflects the Imam's genuine conviction and theological position
key_terms.خِلَافَ: Contrary to / different from — describes apparent discrepancies between Imami narrations that may arise due to taqiyya or different levels of addressees
key_terms.دِفَاعٌ: Defence/protection — referring to the concept of taqiyya (dissimulation), where the Imam speaks something other than the literal truth to protect his followers from harm or to shield sensitive religious knowledge from hostile audiences

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about apparent contradictions in Imami narrations?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) addresses the issue of apparent contradictions in Imami narrations. He explains that when the Imam or Ahlulbayt appear to say something contrary to their established teaching, this is not a genuine contradiction but rather a form of taqiyya — a deliberate protective measure on behalf of the believer. The Imam instructs his followers to hold firm to the verified teachings when they encounter such discrepancies, understanding that the Imam speaks with wisdom concerning their protection.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Nazar Al Khash’amy who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The one who recognises that we<sup>asws</sup> are not saying except for the truth, so let him suffice with what he knows from us<sup>asws</sup>. So if he was to hear from us<sup>asws</sup> different to what he knows, so let him know that, that is a defence from us<sup>asws</sup>, about him’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Nasr al-Kath‘ami who has said the following.

“Abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) has said, ‘Those who know that we say nothing but the truth what they know from us should consider it sufficient. If they would hear from us what is different from what they already know from us they should note that it is our way of defending them.’”
